newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay index ends near day's best, up 1.84 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bombay index ends near day's best, up 1.84 pct.

text.p: Strong local buying helped Bombay shares score a sharp technical rally at the start of the week, reversing three days of declines, dealers said.
"The opening was quite firm and there seems to be reasonable activity in pivotals," said Vetri Subramani, vice-president equity sales at brokerage SSKI Securities.
The Bombay share inde closed 80.86 points, or 1.84 percent, higher at a provisional 4,478.40, near its intra-day high of 4,482.51.
Market-favourite Reliance Industries was a market outperformer Monday, rising 10.50 rupees, or nearly three percent, to end at 381.50 bolstered by foreign fund buying, dealers said.
The rally was largely driven by technical factors after stiff resistance last week when the Bombay index hit a 34-month high, dealers said.
Increased participation from retail investors in a buoyant market will give impetus to a rise in mid-cap shares, they said.

"Shares are likely to perform well and should deliver higher returns than fixed income investments over the next two to three years," Kothari Pioneer AMC, the Indian affiliate of Pioneer Group Inc of the United States, said in its annual investment review.
"The catalyst should come from overseas with many foreign funds seeking to increase their India weighting by channelling more assets to us."

Easing of redemption pressures faced by major domestic mutual funds, an expected improvement in corporate profitability after a reduction in interest rates and the return of domestic investors will lead to a broad-based rally in share prices, Kothari said.

"During this process, we believe that the time wil soon come when the large-cap stocks become so overvalued that it will make compelling sense to look at the next tier of slightly less liquid, medium-sized company shares."
